task.title: A city redevelopment project
task.scenario: A newspaper has asked readers to evaluate a new development that turned an old factory into homes, shops and a park.
task.prompt: Write an article for the newspaper evaluating a major building or city project in your country or region. Say whether it was a good decision.
instructions: Make sure you cover all of the points below.
You are writing for: newspaper readers. Style: semi-formal to formal.

expected_response.discourse_complexity: Structured multi-paragraph text or an extended, organised turn.
expected_response.linguistic_demand: Developed, structured discourse; argument with supporting detail; evaluation of options; complex sentences and a range of cohesive devices.
expected_response.cognitive_demand: Weigh advantages and disadvantages; Describe people, places, objects, routines

examples.label: Illustrative outline only - not an answer key; many other responses are equally valid

learning_objectives.text: Write an evaluative article that describes, analyses and judges

difficulty.language_demand: Developed, structured discourse; argument with supporting detail; evaluation of options; complex sentences and a range of cohesive devices.
difficulty.cognitive_demand: Weigh advantages and disadvantages; Describe people, places, objects, routines
expected_performance: Addresses all parts of the task in a developed way; position or purpose is clear throughout; ideas are relevant and extended with examples.
Information arranged logically; a range of cohesive devices used appropriately; clear progression within paragraphs.
Good range with some precision; uses collocation and word formation; errors are occasional and do not obscure meaning.
difficulty.rationale: Heuristic components (0=A1 .. 5=C2): {'grammar': 2.5, 'cognition': 1.5, 'length': 2.95, 'abstractness': 3.2, 'prompt_language': 1.38}; composite 2.3 -> B1. Original target B2. Computed from invited grammar, cognitive operations, expected length, abstractness and prompt language only.

criteria.name: Task fulfilment
criteria.description: How fully and appropriately the response does what the task asks: required points, purpose, audience and, where relevant, position.
criteria.successful_performance: Addresses all parts of the task in a developed way; position or purpose is clear throughout; ideas are relevant and extended with examples. Required points: describe the project briefly; analyse benefits for residents; discuss any drawbacks; give a final judgement
criteria.weak_performance: A part of the task is ignored or only briefly treated; position unclear or inconsistent; ideas general and unsupported.
criteria.expected_evidence: Which required points are present; how each is supported; whether purpose, audience and position are clear. Check each required point: describe the project briefly; analyse benefits for residents; discuss any drawbacks; give a final judgement.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Content knowledge is not assessed; do not penalise factual inaccuracy unless the task asks for accuracy to a supplied source.

criteria.name: Coherence and cohesion
criteria.description: How logically the ideas connect and how clearly linking devices and reference express those connections.
criteria.successful_performance: Information arranged logically; a range of cohesive devices used appropriately; clear progression within paragraphs.
criteria.weak_performance: Mechanical or overused linkers; unclear reference; weak paragraph logic.
criteria.expected_evidence: Order of ideas; variety and accuracy of linkers; clarity of pronoun reference; paragraph logic.
common_error_patterns: misuse of however / on the other hand
criteria.evaluation_limitations: A text can be cohesive and still weak on content; keep this criterion separate from task fulfilment.

criteria.name: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Range, precision and appropriateness of vocabulary, including collocation and word formation.
criteria.successful_performance: Good range with some precision; uses collocation and word formation; errors are occasional and do not obscure meaning.
criteria.weak_performance: Limited precision; repeated phrases; noticeable collocation or word-form errors.
criteria.expected_evidence: Range of topic words; repetition; collocation; word formation; spelling. Expected vocabulary demands: urban planning; construction and design; evaluation language.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not reward unusual words that are used incorrectly; do not penalise a plain word that is correct and appropriate.

patterns: relative clause pronoun repetition ('the man who he ...')
overuse of 'and' as a clause linker
l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Range of structures used and the accuracy with which they are controlled, including punctuation that affects clarity.
criteria.successful_performance: Variety of complex structures; most sentences error-free; errors persist in less common structures.
criteria.weak_performance: Errors in complex structures reduce clarity at times; reliance on a few patterns.
criteria.expected_evidence: Types of structures; proportion of error-free sentences; kinds of errors; whether errors are systematic. Structures invited by the task: passive_voice, relative_clauses, contrast_and_concession, present_perfect.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Judge by the structures the learner chooses and controls; do not penalise absence of structures the task does not invite.

patterns: relative clause pronoun repetition ('the man who he ...')
overuse of 'and' as a clause linker
l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Register and appropriateness
criteria.description: Whether tone, formality, conventions of text type and politeness suit the audience and purpose.
criteria.successful_performance: Register consistently appropriate; conventions of the text type controlled; tone suits purpose. Audience: newspaper readers. Register: semi-formal to formal
criteria.weak_performance: Slips into informal expressions in formal text; weak politeness strategies.
criteria.expected_evidence: Greeting/closing; politeness markers; formality of vocabulary and structures; conventions.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Only scored where the task defines an audience/register; otherwise treat as not applicable.

not_assessed_by_design.name: Organisation and development of ideas
not_assessed_by_design.reason: Not required by this task type at this level, so it must not be used to reduce the score.

required_demonstrations: Address every required point: describe the project briefly; analyse benefits for residents; discuss any drawbacks; give a final judgement
Use language appropriate to: newspaper readers
not_penalised: absence of C1/C2 devices (cleft sentences, subjunctive)
idiomatic language that is not required
factual inaccuracy about the topic (content knowledge is not assessed)

policy.observed_error_vs_weakness: A diagnostic category is an OBSERVED error pattern when at least one instance is found in a response. It may be reported as an INFERRED learning weakness only after >= 3 instances in one response set of >= 100 words (or >= 2 responses) and when the error is not explained by task demands (for example a tense the task did not invite).

diagnostics.observed_vs_inferred: An error is OBSERVED when an instance appears in the response. It may be recorded as an INFERRED weakness only under the policy in diagnostics.policy (repeated instances, enough text, and not explained by task demands).
